title: Savoury Cabbage Omelette
subtitle: Japanese-inspired pancake with cabbage and spring onion
excerpt: This savoury egg and cabbage pancake takes its cue from okonomiyaki, the beloved Japanese street food. The batter is simple and the result is crisp on the outside, soft and custardy within. It is a satisfying meatless meal that works for lunch or a light dinner.
sourceNotes: Okonomiyaki is a Japanese savoury pancake whose name means 'cook what you like'. It is most closely associated with Osaka and Hiroshima, where distinct regional styles have developed over the twentieth century.

content.text: Shred the cabbage as finely as you can. Thick pieces won't soften through the batter and the texture will be uneven. This makes 4 individual pancakes; cook them one at a time and keep finished ones warm in a low oven.
Put the flour in a large bowl. Whisk in the beaten eggs until you have a smooth batter. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil and mix well.
Fold in the shredded cabbage and spring onions. The batter will be very thick and cabbage-heavy. This is correct.
Heat a little oil in a medium frying pan over a medium heat. Spoon in a quarter of the mixture and press gently into a round about 1.5cm thick.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the underside is deep golden. Flip carefully and cook for another 4 minutes. Repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve with extra soy sauce for dipping.

items.cause: Underside not fully set before turning.
items.fix: Cook for 2 more minutes on low heat before flipping.

items.symptom: Centre is raw even when outside is golden
items.cause: Pancake too thick or heat too high.
items.fix: Press thinner and cook on lower heat with a lid on.
